==Problem==
Tyler is tiling the floor of his 12-foot by 16-foot living room. He plans to place one-foot by one-foot square tiles to form a border along the edges of the room and to fill in the rest of the floor with two-foot by two-foot square tiles. How many tiles will he use?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }48\qquad\textbf{(B) }87\qquad\textbf{(C) }89\qquad\textbf{(D) }96\qquad \textbf{(E) }120</imath>

==Solution 1==

He will place <imath>(12\cdot2)+((16-2)\cdot2)=52</imath> tiles around the border. For the inner part of the room, we have <imath>10\cdot14=140</imath> square feet. Each tile takes up <imath>2^{2}</imath>, or <imath>4</imath> square feet, so he will use <imath>\frac{140}{4}=35</imath> tiles for the inner part of the room. Thus, the answer is <imath>52+35= \boxed{\textbf{(B) }87}</imath>.

~small edit by i_am_not_suk_at_math

~minor edit by Flexo3168

==Solution 2==
The area around the border: <math>(12 \cdot 2) + (14 \cdot 2) = 52</math>. The area of tiles around the border: <math>1 \cdot 1 = 1</math>. Therefore, <math>\frac{52}{1} = 52</math> is the number of tiles around the border.

The inner part will have <math>(12 - 2)(16 - 2) = 140</math>. The area of those tiles are <math>2 \cdot 2 = 4</math>. <math>\frac{140}{4} = 35</math> is the amount of tiles for the inner part. So, <math>52 + 35 = \boxed{87}</math>.
